basis: Neuronopathic storage disease with defining splenic/marrow involvement; destructive bone disease 80-99%. Hepatic storage and aortic calcification omitted at cap; gaze palsy is neurologic.

decisions.haematologic: primary: macrophage storage in spleen and marrow with cytopenias is a defining systemic component; the blood-organ mechanism rule applies.

basis: Herniation of intracranial contents through a congenital skull-base bony defect defines basal encephalocele.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: the skull-base bone defect is an essential anatomical component of the malformation.

basis: Mitochondrial neurologic disease with defining ptosis/ophthalmoplegia; optic atrophy and myopathy each occur in 30-79%. Predominantly valproate-associated hepatic failure excluded.

decisions.ocular: primary: ptosis and external ophthalmoplegia are explicitly defining manifestations; optic atrophy in 30-79% additionally establishes direct ocular injury.

basis: Autoimmune hypercoagulability with defining arterial/venous thrombosis. Stroke is separately diagnosed despite HPO frequency of 30-79%; livedo alone does not establish skin damage.

decisions.neurologic: none: ischemic stroke is a separately diagnosed thrombotic complication, excluded by the separate-disease rule despite its 30-79% HPO frequency.

basis: Developmental impairment defines syndrome; hypodontia and brachydactyly 80-99%, kyphoscoliosis 30-79%, ptosis 5/7. Hypertension is a separate diagnosis; external-ear shape alone adds no axis.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: brachydactyly occurs in 80-99% and kyphoscoliosis in 30-79%; these are associated skeletal malformations rather than the syndrome's defining organ.

basis: Toxic basal-ganglia encephalopathy defines manganism. Visual impairment occurs in 30-79%, but direct ocular injury is unestablished; inhalation alone does not establish lung damage.

decisions.ocular: none: visual impairment in 30-79% does not localize injury to the eye or optic nerve; central visual dysfunction remains possible.

basis: Developmental impairment and brittle/fine hair define syndrome; fine hair in 3/4. Type 2 diabetes in 2/4 is separately diagnosed without established direct endocrine injury; aneurysm in 1/4.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: type 2 diabetes in 2/4 meets the frequency threshold, but the evidence does not establish direct syndromic endocrine injury rather than a separate disease.

basis: Mandibular defects, deafness and lipodystrophic endocrinopathy define MDPL; dermal/subcutaneous atrophy 4/4. Hepatic steatosis 2/3 and dental crowding 4/4 omitted at cap.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: dermal and subcutaneous atrophy affects 4/4; the three primary slots cover named skeletal/hearing disease and the required metabolic mechanism.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this is a lipodystrophic metabolic disorder with insulin resistance in 4/4, hypertriglyceridemia in 3/4 and hypogonadism in 3/3 assessed males.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment, developmental cataracts and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism define Martsolf syndrome; persistent camptodactyly occurs in 1/1 assessed patient, with limited precision.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent camptodactyly is direct structural involvement, reported in 1/1 assessed patient; supplied HPO supports inclusion despite the small denominator.

basis: Localized skin absence defines ACC. Calvarial defects occur in roughly 20% and spinal dysraphism is uncommon; supplied 80-99% annotations conflict with the umbrella phenotype and definition.

decisions.neurologic: none: spinal dysraphism is an uncommon associated anomaly, below 30%; the 80-99% annotation conflicts with usual ACC and the definition's occasional anomalies.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: underlying calvarial defects occur in roughly 20%, below threshold; the supplied 80-99% annotation does not represent the usual umbrella phenotype.
